title: Stage 2: Relationships
summary: Authors with many books, members, and loans as a join entity between members and books.

steps.title: Authors, members, loans
body: - an **author** writes many **books**; every book has exactly one author (a required foreign key `AuthorId`),

- a **member** borrows many books, and a book is borrowed by many members over time. A loan has data of its own (a due date, whether it was returned), so it is an explicit **join entity**, `Loan`, with `BookId` and `MemberId`.
Two design decisions for this stage:

1. **Responses are projections**, not entities. Serialising an entity that has navigations (`Book.Author`, `Author.Books`) can loop forever or leak columns. A small record such as `BookRow(Id, Title, Isbn, Year, Author)` says exactly what the API returns, and the `Select` that builds it also writes the join.
2. **Members are never cascade-deleted with their loan history by accident**: the `Loan → Member` relationship uses `DeleteBehavior.Restrict`. Stage 6 deletes members on purpose.

steps.prompt: `GET /books` should show each book's author name. Which query fits best?
options: `db.Books.Select(b => new BookRow(b.Id, b.Title, b.Isbn, b.Year, b.Author.Name)).ToList()`
`db.Books.ToList()` then look up each author with `Find`
steps.explain: The projection runs one query with a join and returns exactly the API's shape. Returning entities with `Include` serialises `Author.Books` back again (a cycle), and looking up each author is N+1.

steps.explain: The member side was configured with `Restrict`, so deleting a member with loans fails. The book side kept the default for a required key, `Cascade`.

steps.title: Authors, members and loans
prompt: Keep everything from stage 1 and grow the model. Every response is now a **projection**.
- `Book` gains a required `int AuthorId` and `Author Author`, and `List<Loan> Loans`.
- `Loan`: `Id`, `BookId`/`Book`, `MemberId`/`Member`, `DateOnly Due`, `bool Returned`. The member relationship uses `OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict)`.
- `POST /authors` `{ name }`: `201` with `{ id, name }`; `400` for a blank name.
- `GET /authors/{id}`: `{ id, name, books: ["Earthsea", ...] }` (titles alphabetical) with **one** projection; `404` if missing.

- `POST /books` now takes `authorId` too (`record NewBook(string? Title, string? Isbn, int Year, int AuthorId)`); `400` for an unknown author; the response and both `GET /books` endpoints return `record BookRow(int Id, string Title, string Isbn, int Year, string Author)` (the author's name).
- `POST /members` `{ name, email }`: `201` with `{ id, name, email }`; `400` if either is blank or the email has no `@`; `409` if the email is taken.

static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("authors, books and members", async () =>
var dojoA = await Post(http, "/authors", new { name = "Frank Herbert" });
DojoWeb.Status("POST /authors responds 201", 201, dojoA);
Dojo.Eq("the first author gets id 1", "1", await Id(dojoA));
await Post(http, "/authors", new { name = "Ursula K. Le Guin" });
DojoWeb.Status("an author with no name: 400", 400, await Post(http, "/authors", new { name = " " }));
var dojoB = await Post(http, "/books", new { title = "Dune", isbn = "9780441013593", year = 1965, authorId = 1 });
DojoWeb.Status("POST /books with an author responds 201", 201, dojoB);
Dojo.Eq("...and names the author", "Frank Herbert", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(dojoB), "author"));
await Post(http, "/books", new { title = "The Dispossessed", isbn = "9780547773742", year = 1974, authorId = 2 });
await Post(http, "/books", new { title = "Earthsea", isbn = "9780061054884", year = 1968, authorId = 2 });
DojoWeb.Status("an unknown author: 400", 400, await Post(http, "/books", new { title = "X", isbn = "9780441104024", year = 1, authorId = 9 }));
DojoWeb.Status("a duplicate isbn is still 409", 409, await Post(http, "/books", new { title = "X", isbn = "9780441013593", year = 1, authorId = 1 }));
var dojoList = await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync("/books"));
Dojo.Eq("GET /books shows each author", "Frank Herbert|Ursula K. Le Guin|Ursula K. Le Guin", Each(dojoList, "author"));
Dojo.Eq("GET /books/3 has the author", "Ursula K. Le Guin", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync("/books/3")), "author"));
var dojoAuthor = await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync("/authors/2"));
Dojo.Eq("GET /authors/2 lists the titles alphabetically", "Earthsea,The Dispossessed",
Field(dojoAuthor, "books") is { ValueKind: JsonValueKind.Array } dojoBooks ? string.Join(",", dojoBooks.EnumerateArray().Select(b => b.GetString())) : "(no books array)");
DojoWeb.Status("GET /authors/9 responds 404", 404, await http.GetAsync("/authors/9"));
DojoWeb.Status("POST /members responds 201", 201, await Post(http, "/members", new { name = "Ana", email = "ana@example.com" }));
DojoWeb.Status("the same email again: 409", 409, await Post(http, "/members", new { name = "Ana B", email = "ana@example.com" }));
DojoWeb.Status("an email without @: 400", 400, await Post(http, "/members", new { name = "Ben", email = "ben" }));
static async Task<HttpResponseMessage> Post(HttpClient http, string url, object body) => await http.PostAsJsonAsync(url, body);
static async Task<string?> Id(HttpResponseMessage r) => DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(r), "id");
static string Each(JsonElement json, string prop) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array ? string.Join("|", json.EnumerateArray().Select(x => DojoWeb.Prop(x, prop))) : "(not an array)";
static JsonElement Field(JsonElement json, string name)
if (json.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Object) return default;
foreach (var p in json.EnumerateObject()) if (string.Equals(p.Name, name, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) return p.Value;
return default;
